problem: S3-SECU-01: `report.bytesMissing += entry.byteSize ?? 0` is a plain, trapping Int64 addition over byte sizes the manifest declares. Every other figure built from manifest sizes saturates (PlanBuilder.adding, InFlightBytes, addingSaturating in 26 places, SizeGuard, PackProgressScaler), and the transport explicitly supports `maxAssetBytes = Int64.max` meaning 'unlimited' (Tests/ZTronAssetTransportTests/ArithmeticSafetyTests.swift:100, extremeConfiguredCaps). With that public configuration (AssetClientConfiguration.limits), a manifest whose missing entries declare sizes summing past Int64.max (two entries of 2^62 bytes are enough) crashes the process on the first availability(scope:) or ensureAvailable(scope:) call. The path is AssetClient.availability (AssetClient.swift:210) → SyncEngine.performAvailability → store.availability, and EngineCommands.swift:601/705 for ensureAvailable. The default limits cannot overflow, because 100,000 × 4 GiB is below Int64.max. The crash needs maxAssetBytes × maxEntries > Int64.max, so it is reachable only under a non-default but documented and tested configuration.
fix: Saturate both additions in `currentAvailability(of:)` (`AssetStore+Reads.swift:70`, `:85`) with the store's existing `Int64.addingSaturating`; the probe becomes the regression test (expects `bytesMissing == Int64.max`, `missing == 2`). Check every other sum over manifest-declared sizes in WP-B's files for the same trap and list them in the draft.

problem: S3-CONF-06: When an apply changes an asset's checksum to bytes another asset already holds, adoptKnownBlob binds the record to the live blob. It then releases the record's previous blob (`if let previous, previous != key { releaseReference(previous, dooming: .unreferenced) }`), and that release is the only thing that ever schedules the old blob for pruning. The line has 0 executions in the suite. A mutant that removes the release leaves the old blob on disk with a live blob-table entry and no record, so the reaper and orphan GC never collect it. That is an undetected R-CLN-1 violation.
fix: Test the release of the old blob when a content change adopts bytes another asset already holds (`AssetStore+Apply.swift:345-346`, count 0); the confirmer's mutant (`confirm-conformance/S3-CONF-02-06.mutants.sh`) must fail it.

problem: S3-PERF-04: The queue is an ArraySlice. With 64-key batches and the 1 ms unit time budget (ADR draft B-10), a unit attempts about 20 keys. The about 44 keys it did not attempt are each put back with queue.insert near the front, which shifts the whole remaining queue every time. The reclaim's actor work is therefore O(n squared / unit size). At 10,000 blobs it is within P-13's 2.0 s total, but the total doubles roughly 3x per doubling of the set.
fix: Make the reaper's handling of keys a unit did not attempt linear (`AssetStore+Reaper.swift:193`; the confirmer's cursor experiment `confirm-performance/S3-PERF-04-cursor-reaper-experiment.diff` measured linear scaling). Pin it with a deterministic structural test (operations per key) and record the release measurement at 10k/20k/40k.

detail.fix: Keep the sorted queue as an Array with a cursor. Build each batch from the cursor without consuming it, and after the unit advance the cursor by outcome.attempted only. The keys that were not attempted, put back to doomed, stay in place and are re-validated by the next batch's deletionBlocker check. This costs O(1) per key and keeps the order unchanged.

detail.repro: swiftc -O -swift-version 5 S3-PERF-03-P13UnlinkProbe-main.swift -o p13probe && ./p13probe <dir on the repo volume> 10000 matrix   (subsets: control | interleaved | userInteractive | period)
detail.fix:
No code change removes the stall. It sits inside one unlink(2) and recurs by count, so smaller units, rate limiting, pre-syncing blobs and fan-out changes do not avoid it. Raising the deletion queue's QoS only removes the preemption share under load, at an energy cost for background GC. Options for the owner:
(B, robust) Raise batch_ms_max to about 15 ms. One stall (up to about 11 ms in ADR-050's quiet runs, 6.6 ms here) plus the 1 ms unit budget fits.
(A, marginal) Judge the per-batch bound on a percentile. At about 1 stall per 900 unlinks and about 20 unlinks per unit, 1.5-2 % of units contain one, so p99 passes only when fewer than half of the stalls exceed the 4 ms headroom. p98 would be robust.
(C) Judge the batch bound on what it protects. Units run on the dedicated metadata DispatchQueue, so a stalled unlink holds neither the store's actor nor a cooperative-pool thread. The bound would be the longest actor hold between units (as StorageBenchmarks.actorStretches measures) plus unit on-CPU time, with the wall-clock maximum printed as information.
All three are SPEC 6 or quality-gates decisions; nothing was edited (G1).

location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Store/AssetStore+Snapshot.swift:15-21 (refreshPresentEntry) and :43-49 (installSnapshot shares presentTable as the snapshot's entries); Store/AssetStore+Publish.swift:172
problem: S3-PERF-05: A .userInitiated publication installs at once. The snapshot's entries is the store's presentTable, shared copy-on-write, and the sink (SnapshotMirror) keeps it. The next publication's refreshPresentEntry therefore copies the whole present table, retaining an id, a URL and an extension per entry, on the store's actor. A run of n user-initiated publications, such as ensureAvailable over a scope, costs O(n squared). Bulk and prefetch publications install at most every snapshotInstallInterval and do not pay this. The cause is inferred from the code; the probe proves the superlinear cost.
fix: User-initiated publications copy the present table, so a long run of them is quadratic (10,000: 4.9 s; bulk is linear). Record with the measurement. OPTIONAL fix only if a bounded, low-risk design exists in WP-B's files (for example a small overlay on the snapshot compacted periodically).

detail.fix: Make a user-initiated install O(changes) instead of O(present). Give AssetSnapshot a shared, rarely rebuilt base table plus a small overlay of the entries changed since the base. Lookup reads the overlay first, which stays O(1). Rebuild the base off the hot path when the overlay passes about sqrt(n) entries. Alternatively, double-buffer the present table using ack.retired, which the store already receives back. Keep the 'installed before publish returns' contract.

confirmer.reason:
Reproduced in release at load 63.8 to 70.3. The probe failed at S3PerfPublishProbe.swift:29. User-initiated runs: 2.5k 0.51 s, 5k 1.72 s, 10k 4.92 s, a 10k/5k ratio of 2.86. Bulk: ratio 2.11.

The hunter inferred the cause from code. I tested it with a control sink that acknowledges without retaining the snapshot, so presentTable is uniquely referenced again after install. User-initiated publications then scaled linearly (0.42, 1.07, 2.14 s, ratio 2.00), against 2.75 with the retaining sink in the same run. The copy-on-write copy of the shared presentTable (AssetStore+Snapshot.swift:15-21 and :43-49; ScriptedSnapshotSink and SnapshotMirror keep `current`) is the cause.

The per-publication cost at 10,000 is about 0.5 to 1 ms, so there is no C2 breach. No SPEC 6 budget applies, and the P-4 ratio is borrowed for the probe. DECISIONS.md already lists 'WP-B's present-table copy' under the Stage 3 hardening item (1) at maxEntries; the quadratic cost over a run of publications is the new angle. Non-blocking. The owner is WP-B.
